summary: This is a Makefile target named 'helloWorld' that, when invoked, executes a simple echo command to print 'Hello World' to the console. It's a basic example of how to define and run tasks in a Makefile.

explanations.1: The colon after 'helloWorld' defines this as a Makefile target — a named task you can run by typing 'make helloWorld' at the command line.
explanations.2: The tab character at the start is required by Makefile syntax; it tells Make that this line is a command to execute, not part of the target declaration. Without it, Make will error out.
